title: GMAT Focus Quant Practice Test 16
instructions: GMAT Focus Edition Quantitative Reasoning: 21 Problem Solving questions, 45 minutes. An on-screen calculator is permitted.

questions.prompt: A town of 25,000 people grows by 20% a year. What is its population after 2 years?
questions.explanation: After one year the town holds 30,000, and 20% of that is 6,000 more: 36,000. Applying 20% twice to the original figure gives 35,000 and misses the growth on the first year's growth.

questions.prompt: Solve for x: (x + 3) / 4 = (2x − 6) / 5
questions.explanation: Multiplying both sides by 20 clears the fractions: 5(x + 3) = 4(2x − 6), so 5x + 15 = 8x − 24. Taking 5x from each side leaves 3x − 24 = 15, and adding 24 gives 3x = 39, so x = 13.

questions.prompt: A set of numbers has a mean of 24. Every number is halved and then increased by 3. What is the new mean?
questions.explanation: Halving every value halves the mean, to 12, and adding 3 to every value adds 3 to the mean: 15. Adding first and then halving gives 13.5, which applies the two steps in the wrong order.

questions.prompt: A chord of a circle subtends an angle of 40 degrees at a point on the circumference. What angle does it subtend at the centre?
questions.explanation: The angle a chord makes at the centre is twice the angle it makes at any point on the remaining circumference: 2 × 40 = 80 degrees. 20 degrees halves it instead of doubling, and 40 degrees assumes the two angles are equal.

questions.prompt: Two numbers are in the ratio 5 : 7. When 5 is added to each, the ratio becomes 3 : 4. What is the smaller of the original numbers?
questions.explanation: Write the numbers as 5k and 7k. Then (5k + 5) / (7k + 5) = 3/4, which gives 20k + 20 = 21k + 15, so k = 5. The numbers are 25 and 35, and adding 5 to each gives 30 and 40, which is indeed 3 : 4.

questions.prompt: What is the value of (3 × 10⁵) × (4 × 10⁻²)?
questions.explanation: Multiply the numbers and add the indices: 3 × 4 = 12, and 10⁵ × 10⁻² = 10³. So the answer is 12 × 10³ = 12,000. Subtracting the indices instead of adding gives 10⁷ and an answer of 12,000,000.

questions.prompt: A spinner has 8 equal sectors, 3 of them red. It is spun twice. What is the probability of at least one red?
questions.explanation: The chance of missing red on one spin is 5/8, so the chance of missing it twice is (5/8)² = 25/64. At least one red is everything else: 1 − 25/64 = 39/64. Doubling the single-spin chance gives 6/8, which double-counts the case where both spins are red.

questions.prompt: 12 items are bought for £96.00 in total and sold at £11.00 each. What is the profit as a percentage of cost?
questions.explanation: The 12 items sell for £132.00 against a cost of £96.00, a profit of £36.00. As a percentage of cost that is 37.5%. Measuring the same profit against the selling price gives 27.27%, a different question.

questions.prompt: A tank fills at 20 litres a minute for 15 minutes, and then at 35 litres a minute until it holds 1,000 litres. How long does the whole filling take?
questions.explanation: The first stage puts in 20 × 15 = 300 litres, leaving 700 litres to go at 35 litres a minute: 20 minutes. The whole filling therefore takes 15 + 20 = 35 minutes. 20 minutes counts only the second stage.

questions.prompt: Taking pi as 22/7, a closed cylinder has a radius of 7 cm and a height of 10 cm. What is its total surface area?
questions.explanation: The curved surface is 2 pi r h = 440 cm², and the two circular ends add 2 pi r² = 308 cm², giving 748 cm² in all. 440 cm² is the curved surface alone, which would be right only for an open tube.

questions.prompt: What is the value of 87² − 13²?
questions.explanation: Rather than squaring both numbers, use the difference of two squares: 87² − 13² = (87 + 13)(87 − 13) = 100 × 74 = 7,400. Squaring the difference instead gives 5,476, and multiplying the two numbers gives 1,131 — neither is the difference of the squares.

questions.prompt: A rota runs 4 days on and 2 days off, repeating. How many working days fall in the first 30 days?
questions.explanation: The rota repeats every 6 days, and 30 days is exactly 5 full cycles. Each cycle contains 4 working days, so there are 5 × 4 = 20. 10 is the number of days off.

questions.prompt: One pound buys 1.24 dollars, and one dollar buys 0.82 euros. How many euros does £500.00 buy?
questions.explanation: £500.00 buys 620 dollars, and each dollar buys 0.82 euros: 620 × 0.82 = 508.40 euros. Dividing by 0.82 instead of multiplying gives 756.10 euros, which would be right only if euros were worth more than dollars.

questions.prompt: A machine loses 20% of its value every year. After how many whole years is it worth less than half what it cost?
questions.explanation: After 3 years the machine holds 51.2% of its value, still above half; after 4 years it holds 40.96%, which is below. So 4 years is the first whole year at which it is worth less than half. Losing 20% five times over would be 100% and is not how compounding works.

questions.prompt: Five numbers are 22, 28, 31, 35, 39. A sixth number is added and the mean is unchanged. What is the sixth number?
questions.explanation: The five total 155, so their mean is 31. For six numbers to keep that mean they must total 186, so the sixth is 186 − 155 = 31. Adding a value equal to the mean always leaves the mean where it was; adding zero would drag it down.

questions.prompt: A square has an area of 72 cm². What is the length of its diagonal?
questions.explanation: The diagonal splits the square into two right-angled triangles, and the area of a square is also half the square of its diagonal: d² = 2 × 72 = 144, so d = 12 cm. 8.49 cm is the side, which is shorter than the diagonal.

questions.prompt: A tank holding 900 litres when full is two thirds full. A pump removes 25 litres a minute. How long does it take to empty?
questions.explanation: Two thirds of 900 litres is 600 litres, and at 25 litres a minute that takes 600 / 25 = 24 minutes. Emptying a full tank would take 36 minutes, which is what using the capacity rather than the contents gives.

questions.prompt: How many different three-digit numbers can be made using the digits 5, 7, 9 once each?
questions.explanation: There are 3 choices for the first digit, 2 for the second and 1 for the last: 3 × 2 × 1 = 6. Allowing digits to repeat would give 3 × 3 × 3 = 27, but the question uses each digit once.

questions.prompt: A value falls by 10% and then rises by 10%. What is the overall change?
questions.explanation: Starting from 100, the fall leaves 90 and the rise takes it to 99 — a net fall of 1%. The two percentages do not cancel, because the rise is taken from the smaller figure the fall left behind.

questions.prompt: If 2x + y = 17 and y = x − 1, what is the value of xy?
questions.explanation: Substituting y = x − 1 into the first equation gives 2x + x − 1 = 17, so 3x = 18 and x = 6. Then y = 5, and xy = 6 × 5 = 30. 11 is the sum of the two values rather than their product.

questions.prompt: An item with a cash price of £950.00 can instead be bought with a deposit of £250.00 and 18 monthly payments of £46.00. How much more does that cost than paying cash?
questions.explanation: The instalments come to 18 × £46.00 = £828.00, and with the deposit the total paid is £1,078.00 — £128.00 more than the cash price. Leaving the deposit out gives £-122.00 and treats the money paid up front as if it were not paid at all.
